payload.text: **BOARD TEXT IS FULL OF BACKTICKS, AND A DOUBLE-QUOTED SHELL ARGUMENT RUNS THEM** (2026-09-17, vc's, recorded here because every node writes board prose this way). vc was composing a board item whose text carried backticked phrases, the shell substituted them, and one of the phrases was vc's rebuild chain: the rebuild fired itself, hours early, from a sentence nobody had run. It happened to be the right rebuild at the right HEAD, so it was let finish -- the harm was luck, not design. **The safe form is the one this board already uses: write the text to a file and pass it as `"$(cat <file>)"`, because a command substitution's OUTPUT is never re-scanned for backticks.** The unsafe form is the inline one, `wb add doing "... \`intent foo\` ..."`, and it is unsafe in exactly the places board prose is richest -- verb names, paths, code spans. Single quotes are also safe but cannot carry an apostrophe, which board prose always has. Same class as watch-out 60's blind replace: the text is data, so move it by file and never through a quoting layer that can execute it.
